match: jsonrpc must be 2.0
rules.reading: A frame whose `jsonrpc` member is not `"2.0"`: one of the JSON-RPC 2.0 rules every message must follow.

match: frame on the protocol channel is not valid JSON-RPC
rules.reading: A frame that does not parse as a JSON-RPC message at all (a non-JSON line, an array, an object of no JSON-RPC shape). A frame that parses but breaks a narrower JSON-RPC rule is left to the rules below.

match: request id has type * MCP requires a string or integer id
rules.reading: A request id that is neither a string nor an integer.

match: request id is null; MCP requires a string or integer id
rules.reading: A request id that is `null`. The message itself names both clauses: `null` is not a string or integer id, and MCP forbids it outright.

match: request reuses an id already in flight
rules.reading: A request reusing the id of one of its sender's requests that has not been answered. At `2025-11-25` the clause is wider — no reuse within the session at all — and in-flight reuse is the part mcpsnoop checks.

match: response id has no matching request
rules.reading: A response whose id names no outstanding request: the clauses requiring a response to carry the id of the request it answers.

match: duplicate response for the same id
rules.reading: A second response for an id already answered, which corresponds to no outstanding request.

match: response has neither result nor error
rules.reading: A response carrying neither `result` nor `error`.

match: response has both result and error
rules.reading: A response carrying both `result` and `error`, which JSON-RPC 2.0 forbids. Template read from the binary; no corpus trace exercises it.

match: result is missing required resultType
rules.reading: A result without `resultType`. The field does not exist at `2025-11-25`.

match: client sent a JSON-RPC response, which * no longer defines
rules.reading: A client sending a JSON-RPC response at `2026-07-28`, where a server sends no requests to answer.

match: server sent a JSON-RPC request *, which * replaced with the MRTR pattern
rules.reading: A server-initiated JSON-RPC request at `2026-07-28`, which replaced them with multi round-trip requests.

match: request _meta is missing required io.modelcontextprotocol/
rules.reading: A request without one of the `_meta` fields `2026-07-28` requires on every request.

match: required routing header MCP-Protocol-Version is missing
rules.reading: A POST without the `MCP-Protocol-Version` header where the negotiated revision requires it.

match: required routing header Mcp-Method is missing
required routing header Mcp-Name is missing
rules.reading: A POST without its `Mcp-Method` or `Mcp-Name` request metadata header.

match: required routing header Mcp-Param-* is missing for body parameter
rules.reading: A `tools/call` carrying a parameter its tool marks with `x-mcp-header`, sent without the mirrored `Mcp-Param-*` header.

match: MCP-Protocol-Version header * disagrees with _meta protocolVersion
rules.reading: An `MCP-Protocol-Version` header that differs from the body's `_meta` protocol version.

match: routing header Mcp-Method * disagrees with body method
rules.reading: An `Mcp-Method` header that is not the body's method. Template read from the binary; no corpus trace exercises it.

match: routing header Mcp-Name * disagrees with body name
rules.reading: An `Mcp-Name` header that is not the body's name after Base64 decoding. It catches an encoding fault only when the fault changes the value: a plain value shaped like the sentinel decodes to something else (TRAN-092), while an unencoded non-ASCII name that equals the body passes (TRAN-077).

match: routing header Mcp-Param-* disagrees with body parameter
rules.reading: An `Mcp-Param-*` header that is not the mirrored body value after Base64 decoding. The encoding clauses are caught only where a fault changes the value (a miscased sentinel does not decode); an unencoded value equal to the body passes.

match: routing header Mcp-Param-* is present but body parameter * is absent or null
rules.reading: An `Mcp-Param-*` header sent although the body parameter is `null` or absent.

match: routing headers are invalid on a JSON-RPC batch
rules.reading: Routing headers on a POST whose body is a batch. Template read from the binary; mcpsnoop reports an HTTP batch only when routing headers ride it.

match: a routing header disagrees with the body
rules.reading: The server answered `-32020` (`HeaderMismatch`). mcpsnoop counts the rejection itself as the routing fault, which convicts the client's headers on the server's word.

match: the response to a request * the transport * application/json or text/event-stream
rules.reading: A POST carrying a request answered with a `Content-Type` other than `application/json` or `text/event-stream`, or with none.

match: cacheable * result declares no ttlMs, which * requires
rules.reading: A complete result of a cacheable operation without `ttlMs`. CACH-001 asks for caching hints; mcpsnoop checks `ttlMs` and not `cacheScope`.

match: cacheScope * on a later page of * disagrees with
rules.reading: Pages of one list request carrying different `cacheScope` values.

match: cacheScope is *, and * defines only public and private
rules.reading: A `cacheScope` outside `public` and `private`. No RFC 2119 clause states the enumeration; the revision's JSON Schema does, which the report judges as its wire schema.

match: ttlMs is *, and * requires a value of zero or more
rules.reading: A negative `ttlMs`.

match: InputRequiredResult carries neither inputRequests nor requestState
rules.reading: An `InputRequiredResult` with neither `inputRequests` nor `requestState`.

match: InputRequiredResult on *, which * allows only on
rules.reading: An `InputRequiredResult` answering a method that may not return one.

match: inputRequests names *, and * allows only
rules.reading: An `inputRequests` entry that is not an elicitation, sampling or roots request.

match: inputRequests asks for * while the request declared no
rules.reading: An `inputRequests` entry for a capability the request did not declare at all. A declared capability whose mode or sub-capability is missing (URL-mode elicitation, `sampling.tools`) is not compared.

match: MRTR retry changed requestState
rules.reading: A retry echoing a `requestState` other than the one the server sent.

match: MRTR retry is missing requestState
rules.reading: A retry leaving out the `requestState` the server sent. Template read from the binary; no corpus trace exercises it.

match: MRTR retry invented requestState
rules.reading: A retry carrying a `requestState` the server never sent.

match: arrived on subscription * before its acknowledgment
rules.reading: A subscription notification sent before the subscription's acknowledgment.

match: carries no io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId
rules.reading: A notification on a subscription stream without `io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId`. BASE-039 also requires the id to be the stream's own; mcpsnoop checks presence.

match: was not requested by subscription
rules.reading: A notification type the subscription did not ask for. SUBS-001 binds every notification the server sends; mcpsnoop checks those that carry a subscription id.

match: progress for token * went from * requires it to increase
rules.reading: A progress value that does not increase.

match: progress notification for token * arrived after its request completed
rules.reading: A progress notification after its request was answered.

match: server cancelled *, and * lets a server cancel only a subscriptions/listen request
rules.reading: A server-sent `notifications/cancelled` naming anything but a `subscriptions/listen` request.

match: advertises an inputSchema that is not a JSON object
rules.reading: A tool whose `inputSchema` is not a JSON Schema object.

match: declares an x-mcp-header under *, which * does not allow in the chain
rules.reading: An `x-mcp-header` on a property not reachable through `properties` alone.

match: declares x-mcp-header * on more than one property
rules.reading: One `x-mcp-header` name on two properties of a tool: one of the constraints TRAN-080 lists.

match: a task handle uses the io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks extension, which the client never advertised
rules.reading: A `CreateTaskResult` answering a request whose client capabilities do not declare the tasks extension. The tasks extension's own clause, TASK-001 — reported in the extension's block and never scored — names exactly this; mcpsnoop cites the core negotiation clause VERS-005, of which it is one case and which our registry excludes because each extension, not the core, says what falling back means.
